title: A notebook of questions: one question a day
description: Not answers — questions. A notebook that collects one genuine question a day becomes, within a year, a map of what your mind actually wonders about.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Questions only
paragraphs: The rule is strict: one question a day, written down, with no obligation to answer it. Why do we dream in colour? Who decides what a word means? The notebook is a commonplace book turned inside out — a collection of not-knowing, kept proudly.

Writing the question matters. A question held only in the head dissolves by bedtime; a question on paper waits patiently, and some questions improve with age, gathering partial answers from books, lessons and conversations you have months later.

body.heading: Reviewing the map
paragraphs: Every few months, read the notebook through. Some questions will have answered themselves. Some will look naive. A few — usually the ones you almost did not write down — will still glow, and those are the ones worth chasing properly.
You will also see your interests drift across the year: a spring of space questions, an autumn of animals. That drift is the real contents page of your curiosity, and no test can show it to you.

takeaway: One unanswered question a day, written down and reviewed every few months, draws a map of your curiosity that nothing else can.
